title: Operation Layout — Pinning Operation Layout
body: Public edition. 'Pinning' is Manon's term, kept as named: a pinning operation is an operation layout in which each work station is 'pinned' to a fixed marked spot on the floor plan so crews, tools, and materials always return to the same place. Layout plan: (1) draw the work area to scale; (2) mark pin spots for each station with numbered floor markers; (3) assign every tool and material bin to a pin; (4) draw the movement arrows between pins in work order; (5) post the pinned layout at the area entrance. Needs list: floor markers or paint, numbered tags, station bins, the scaled plan, tape measures. Rule: nothing moves off its pin without the layout being re-pinned and re-posted.
capabilities: Draw a work area to scale
Draw movement arrows in work order

title: Operation Layout — Oul Operation Layout
body: Public edition. 'Oul' is Manon's term, kept as named: an oul is a named operation cell on a layout grid. An oul operation layout divides the site into letter-numbered cells (A1, A2, B1, B2) and assigns each operation its cells. Layout plan: (1) grid the site into equal cells; (2) label every cell; (3) assign operations to cell ranges; (4) write the needs list per oul — materials, tools, and crew for that cell only; (5) run the day by oul, moving crews cell to cell. Needs list per oul: the cell's materials, its tools, its crew count, and its completion check. Benefit: the needs list is always local — a crew never hunts the whole site for its material.
capabilities: Grid a site into oul cells
Write the needs list per oul

title: Operation Layout — Warehouse Operation Layout
body: Public edition. Public operations reference. A warehouse operation layout pins receiving, storage, picking, packing, and shipping into a one-way flow. Plan: (1) receiving docks on one wall, shipping on the opposite; (2) bulk storage in the middle on racked aisles; (3) fast movers near packing; (4) packing stations between storage and shipping; (5) returns in a quarantined corner. Needs list: pallet racking, forklifts, barcode scanners, packing tables, stretch wrap, labels. Rule: material flows one direction — never let inbound and outbound cross.
capabilities: Lay out the one-way warehouse flow

title: Operation Layout — Workshop Operation Layout
body: Public edition. Public operations reference. A workshop layout groups tools by operation: cutting, shaping, assembly, finishing. Plan: (1) put dust-making tools (saws, sanders) on the dust-collection side; (2) assembly benches in the center with clear walkways; (3) finishing in a clean, ventilated corner; (4) material storage along one wall, cut list posted; (5) sharpening and maintenance at a dedicated station. Needs list: benches, dust collection, clamps, squares, the cut list, first-aid kit. Rule: the dirtiest operation sits farthest from finishing.
capabilities: Post the cut list at storage

title: Operation Layout — Kitchen Operation Layout
body: Public edition. Public operations reference. A commercial kitchen layout follows the food flow: receiving, storage, prep, cooking, plating, service, dish return. Plan: (1) walk-in coolers near receiving; (2) prep tables between storage and the cook line; (3) the cook line (ranges, fryers, ovens) under the hood; (4) plating pass facing service; (5) dish pit on the return path. Needs list: refrigeration, prep tables, cook line equipment, hood suppression, smallwares, thermometers. Rule: raw and ready-to-eat never cross paths.
capabilities: Lay out the food flow line
Place the cook line under the hood

title: Operation Layout — Event Operation Layout
body: Public edition. Public operations reference. An event layout pins entry, registration, main stage, food, restrooms, first aid, and exits. Plan: (1) one controlled entry with bag check; (2) registration just inside; (3) stage with sight lines from all seating; (4) food and water away from the stage sound; (5) restrooms and first aid signed and lit; (6) marked emergency exits on all sides. Needs list: fencing, signage, radios, lighting, generators, water stations, waste bins. Rule: every attendee must see an exit sign from wherever they stand.

title: Operation Layout — Construction Site Operation Layout
body: Public edition. Public operations reference. A construction site layout keeps trades moving: access, laydown, crane, work zones, office, wash. Plan: (1) one construction entrance with wheel wash; (2) laydown yard near the entrance, materials by trade; (3) crane positioned to reach the whole footprint; (4) work zones gridded as ouls; (5) site office and toilets upwind of dust; (6) emergency assembly point marked. Needs list: fencing, signage, crane mats, laydown racking, office trailer, portable toilets, fire extinguishers. Rule: delivery trucks never reverse through work zones.
capabilities: Plan the site entrance and wheel wash
Position the crane for full reach

title: Operation Layout — Needs List Master Method
body: Public edition. Public operations reference. The needs-list master method turns any operation layout into a shopping and staging list. Method: (1) list every operation in work order; (2) under each, list materials with quantities, tools, crew, and time; (3) roll quantities up across operations; (4) mark lead-time items for early order; (5) assign each line to an oul or pin for staging. Needs list columns: item, quantity, unit, operation, oul/pin, lead time, status. Rule: if it is not on the needs list, it does not come to the site.
capabilities: Assign lines to ouls or pins
